complexity.notes: Space can be reduced to O(1) since only ||the two most recent values|| are ever needed, and O(log n) time is achievable via ||fast doubling on the Fibonacci recurrence||. Under the unit-cost model this is O(n) time, but note the digit-level reality: F(n) has Θ(n) bits, so each addition really costs Θ(n) digit work — bit-level cost is O(n^2). The dict works but is overkill here; keys 0..n hash to consecutive slots so lookups are effectively collision-free, and a list would do the same job without hashing at all.
complexity.summary: Iterative bottom-up Fibonacci: seeds a dict with the base cases 0, 1, 2 and fills in each count up to n as the sum of the two previous counts.
